title: Improving the Selection of News Reports for Event Coding Using Ensemble Classification

title: Citizens’ Perceptions of Online Abuse Directed at Politicians: Evidence from a Survey Experiment
notes: Verified 2026-05-04: public tab file has 2,050 respondent rows with numeric message IDs and perception outcomes, but the released data/README do not expose the stimulus text needed for a text-classification task.

title: Online Abuse of Politicians: Experimental Evidence on Politicians’ Own Perceptions
notes: Verified 2026-05-04: public tab file has 9,804 respondent-message rows with numeric message IDs and perception outcomes, but the released data/README do not expose the stimulus text needed for a text-classification task.

title: Political DEBATE / PolNLI

title: Political DEBATE / PolNLI event-detection subset
notes: Staged as `burnham_polnli_event_entailment`, using the event-extraction rows from the public PolNLI test split.

title: Categorizing Topics Versus Inferring Attitudes: A Theory and Method for Analyzing Open-Ended Survey Responses
notes: Best open-ended survey-response direction; likely benchmarkable, but a clean discrete benchmark slice still needs to be chosen.

title: How Populist are Parties? Measuring Degrees of Populism in Party Manifestos Using Supervised Machine Learning
notes: Promising longer-document rhetoric/style candidate, but sentence-level labels may be weaker than ideal.

title: A Text-As-Data Approach for Using Open-Ended Responses as Manipulation Checks
notes: Adds paired prompt-response classification rather than standalone document labeling; may require a discrete benchmark reformulation.

title: Stance detection: a practical guide to classifying political beliefs in text
notes: Useful structured target-conditioned stance candidate, but still lives in the currently overfilled stance family.

title: Automated Dictionary Generation for Political Event Coding
notes: Adds a cyber-incident event domain; replication archive exists, but raw-text readiness still needs inspection.

title: Count Love Protest Dataset
notes: Potentially very practical article-to-event detection resource, but public assets rely on URLs and annotations rather than preserved raw article text.

title: Multilingual Protest News Detection – Shared Task 1, CASE 2021
notes: Interesting multilingual and multi-granularity event benchmark, but weaker on the political-science-paper criterion.

title: We Need to Go Deeper: Measuring Electoral Violence using Convolutional Neural Networks and Social Media
notes: Substantively distinct electoral-violence candidate, but tweet-text public availability is the main risk.

title: Campaign communication and legislative leadership
notes: Implemented in the live manifests as `muller_fujimura_campaign_policy_area`. The public train/test/eval sentence splits expose `policy_area` labels plus statement text directly. The live task uses the combined 2,985-row supervised corpus, drops 12 rows tied to exact-text label conflicts, deduplicates exact repeated text-label pairs, and keeps 2,915 statement-level items across 12 labels including `No Policy Area`.

title: Where do parties talk about what? Party issue salience across communication channels
notes: Multilingual, multi-channel issue-salience dataset; attractive but methodologically closer to Cross-Domain than ideal.

title: Policlim: A Dataset of Climate Change Discourse in the Political Manifestos of Forty-Five Countries from 1990 to 2022
notes: Attractive multilingual climate-policy topic candidate, but narrower than a broad many-topic benchmark.

title: Initiate and Elevate! How Political Parties Can Set an Agenda
notes: Interesting CAP-style macro-issue corpus across modern channels, but machine-assigned labels and news-text access are the main risks.

title: Using Supervised Machine Learning to Code Policy Issues: Can Classifiers Generalize across Contexts?
notes: Good conceptual fit for policy-issue coding, but replication accessibility remains the weak point.

title: TwitCivility Hugging Face release
notes: Staged as `twitcivility_impoliteness`. Public train/test parquet splits contain 13,124 rows with no missing or duplicate text and direct binary labels `impoliteness` and `intolerance`; weaker than Theocharis et al. on the political-science-paper criterion.

title: Benchmarking LLMs in Political Content Text-Annotation: toxicity-protests-ES
notes: Verified 2026-05-04: public CSV has 1,000 Spanish protest-discourse rows with text and two human coder columns plus consensus metadata. Substantively political, direct-label, and useful for multilingual coverage; weaker than paper-backed candidates because it is not a published political-science replication archive.
